text:
incident-bot: Alert: multiple containers on gpu-pool-7 reported CUDA OOM + container restart loop. Auto-scale attempted, some nodes flapped. Investigating memory growth in paged-attention allocator.

maya: saw slow RSS climb on a few hosts, KV cache resident pages growing steadily for ~48h. Not a sudden spike.

raj: logs show repeated `cudaMemcpy` failures then container exited with code 137. stack shows paged_attn::Allocator::alloc at top.

sam: are these all the same model family? any recent deploys?

maya: yes, mostly v2-llama-13b quantized and a small % of v1-replica. No recent runtime pushes in last 6h.

elaine: customer-facing metrics: 0.8% 5xx rate spike for hosted endpoints using those models, latency p95 up ~120ms for affected zones. No data exfiltration.

raj: quick mitigation: temporarily reduce KV cache max_pages and bump eviction aggressiveness. Patch config on affected pool:
```bash
# run on control plane
redwoodctl pools update gpu-pool-7 --set kv_cache.max_pages=500 --set kv_cache.eviction_policy=aggressive
```

maya: started rollout to nodes in pool. Also triggering `restart-service` on the most noisy containers to reclaim fragmented memory.

ops-bot: Deploy started: rollout/1779001234 by maya. 6 nodes to update, sequential. Expected 12m.

sam: can we avoid full restarts for all nodes? want to keep capacity.

maya: doing canary first (node-37), will monitor OOMs/replicas. If steady, continue.

raj: dug into allocator metrics: free slab count trending down, fragmentation ratio up from 0.12 -> 0.44 over 48h. KV page churn low, pages retained due to sticky refs. Possible leak in page pinning path.

elaine: Ops: notify CS about degraded latency + potential rate-limiting fallback for affected customers. Adding to incident status page.

maya: quick hotfix we can do: enable `kv_cache.force_evict=true` and drop sticky TTL to 30s to flush pins. Will cause some regen cost but buys time.

raj: agreed. Pushing flag to pool. Also uploading a small diagnostic: `pmap` and `nvtop` snapshot to S3 at s3://redwood-incident-dumps/1779001234/

ops-bot: Action: flag set and canary restarted (node-37). Monitoring metrics in linked dashboard.

maya: canary looks good for 6m, memory trending down ~700MB, no OOM on that node since restart.

sam: start rolling restarts with 1 node concurrency and health-check gating.

elaine: customer impact update posted. CS contact list informed. No major customers in error spike yet, but some endpoints show >10% increased tail latency.

raj: parallel work: instrument pin/unpin counters and add extra logging if pin_count > 1000 for a single key. Will ship small probe to the cluster after restarts.

maya: handoff for night oncall: watch gpu-pool-7, keep kv_cache.max_pages at 500 until we have allocator fix. If OOMs return, set `kv_cache.disable_paging=true` for the pool and escalate to eng-runtime pager.

sam: noted. Leaving runbook steps in the incident doc: steps to drain node, force-evict, and emergency disable paging.

elaine: postmortem notes to include: slow creep leak in paged-attention allocator, sticky pins preventing eviction, mitigation was config-based eviction + rolling restarts. Impact: transient latency and small 5xx bump.

maya: final: handoff summary -> mitigations applied (reduced max_pages, aggressive eviction, force_evict flag, rolling restarts), canary stable, diagnostics uploaded. Oncall -> sam (night). Escalation path -> pager@eng-runtime, sla owner: raj.

sam: ack, will monitor dashboards and run pin-probe tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
